analysis.one_liner: Ambuja Cements manufactures and sells cement and clinker across India, and is the Adani Group's consolidation platform for its cement business (now absorbing Sanghi, Penna, and in the process of merging with ACC and Orient Cement).
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on October 29, 2026 to approve Q2/H1 FY27 results - the next data point that will show whether margins kept slipping. Separately, the NCLT's final hearing on the Ambuja-ACC merger petition is set for November 19, 2026, part of Adani's plan to fold Ambuja, ACC and Orient Cement into one platform after already absorbing Sanghi Industries and Penna Cement earlier in 2026. Q1 FY27 results (out in July) already showed margins under pressure, and a cement-sector price-fixing probe by the Competition Commission is reportedly close to an order, with a potential penalty near ₹550 crore for Ambuja - not yet confirmed as finalised.
analysis.plain_terms: Ambuja makes cement, and its Adani-group owner has spent heavily over the past two years buying smaller cement makers (Penna, Sanghi, Orient) and is now merging them with sister company ACC into one large entity. The tension: this consolidation story hasn't shown up as better profits yet - fuel and freight costs have squeezed margins, and the cash cushion that used to make Ambuja a famously debt-free company has nearly disappeared. The stock has fallen hard while the wider market has risen, and investors are being asked to trust that cost savings from scale will show up later rather than now.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): standalone revenue ₹6,320 crore, up ~3% YoY, but management flagged this is not strictly comparable to last year because of the Sanghi and Penna amalgamation accounting. Standalone PAT fell 36.6% YoY to ₹504 crore; consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 16.5% from 18.7% a year earlier. Q4 FY26 (March 2026 quarter) looked spectacular on the surface - consolidated PAT up 78.5% YoY to ₹1,830 crore - but this was driven almost entirely by one-off items: a ₹604 crore deferred tax gain and a ₹761 crore tax-provision reversal tied to merger accounting. Strip those out and normalised PAT actually fell 33.5% YoY to ₹569 crore, while EBITDA margin contracted 530bps YoY to 13.4% on higher fuel and freight costs. Treat the headline PAT swings in both quarters as accounting noise, not operating performance.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 47.8% from its July 2024 peak of ₹689 to the last close of ₹360, near its 52-week low of ₹341. There is no demerger or recent split distorting this - the only corporate action on record is a 5:1 split back in 2005 - so this is a genuine, sustained price decline, not an artifact. It has also badly lagged both the market and its closest listed peer: 1-year return -36.5% versus Nifty -9.5%; 3-year -17.7% versus Nifty +16.8% and UltraTech +35.7%; 5-year -8.9% versus Nifty +25.3% and UltraTech +53.8%. This is not a short-term wobble - it is multi-year, broad-based underperformance.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 20.6x, Ambuja trades at about a 30% discount to peer UltraTech's median multiple (~29.5x), and its P/B of ~1.5x is similarly below UltraTech's ~1.74x. The reason it is cheap is explainable: ROE of ~10% and ROCE of ~6.2% are well below what commands a premium multiple in this sector, so the discount reflects genuinely lower returns on capital, not just market mispricing. Whether that makes it cheap in the sense of attractive is a separate question this report does not answer. EV/EBITDA estimates conflicted across sources (9.8x to 12.9x depending on data provider) - not verified precisely, treat as approximate.
analysis.growth_read: Volumes are growing - a record 19.9 million tonnes in Q4 FY26 and 17.1 million tonnes in Q1 FY27, with management targeting 8% volume growth for FY27 and a rising share of trade and premium products. But this volume growth has coincided with, not offset, margin compression (EBITDA margin down 530bps YoY in Q4 FY26, 220bps in Q1 FY27) from fuel, freight and input costs that the company has limited ability to pass through via pricing. So this is volume growth without margin support right now, which in a commodity business like cement is the less durable combination.
analysis.health_read: The clearest concern here is financial, not operational. Ambuja's net cash position - its historical calling card as a debt-free cement major - has collapsed to roughly ₹430 crore as of March 2026, after cash-and-debt-funded acquisitions of Penna Cement (₹10,422 crore enterprise value) and Orient Cement (~₹8,100 crore). Merger-related tax accounting has also made this year's reported profit figures unreliable for judging underlying cash generation - specific free-cash-flow conversion figures are not verified and should be checked on Screener directly. The business itself (cement demand, plant utilisation) looks reasonably stable; the balance-sheet shift from the acquisition spree is the newer and less familiar risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Adani Group, via Holderind Investments ~47.7% and Harmonia Trade and Investment ~19.2%) stands at roughly 67.3%, and the company states no new pledge was created on its shares in FY26. LIC holds a notable 7.28% stake (June 2026) - a well-known, long-standing institutional holder. Beyond LIC and routine mutual fund/DII holdings (~19-20% combined), there is no marquee independent fund manager on the register that stands out; this is largely a promoter-and-institutions-held stock rather than one with a notable outside investor story.
strengths: Trades at roughly a 30% P/E discount to peer UltraTech (20.6x vs ~29.5x)
Record quarterly dispatch volumes - 19.9 million tonnes in Q4 FY26, 17.1 million tonnes in Q1 FY27
Premium product mix rose to 34% of sales (+1pp YoY) and trade share rose 4pp to 78%, both margin-supportive mix shifts
Renewable energy capacity now 973 MW and 34% of the energy mix, part of a stated path to cut total cost to ₹4,250/tonne by FY28
watchpoints: Competition Commission cartelization investigation into major cement makers including Ambuja is reportedly close to an order, with a potential penalty near ₹550 crore - unresolved as of this report
Net cash position fell to roughly ₹430 crore as of March 2026, down sharply from Ambuja's historical large net-cash, debt-free positioning, after heavy M&A spending
EBITDA margin contracted 530bps YoY to 13.4% in Q4 FY26 and further to 16.5% (from 18.7%) in Q1 FY27 on elevated fuel and freight costs

Reported PAT has swung wildly (+78.5% YoY then -34% YoY in consecutive quarters) purely due to one-off merger-related tax accounting - treat headline profit growth/decline figures with caution until normalised
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due October 29, 2026 - specifically whether normalised (ex-one-off) EBITDA margin and PAT stabilise or keep falling, which will show whether the Sanghi/Penna/ACC consolidation is starting to deliver the promised cost synergies (targeted ₹4,250/tonne cost by FY28) or whether margin pressure is structural.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 revenue, EBITDA and PAT figures were cross-checked across Upstox, Free Press Journal and Business Standard, all citing the company's BSE filings; these align. Not reconciled: a stray consolidated PAT figure of ₹660 crore for Q1 FY27 appearing in some secondary aggregators (set aside in favour of the two corroborating primary-sourced figures of ₹577 crore); EV/EBITDA estimates that range from 9.8x to 12.9x across data providers; whether a non-disposal undertaking still applies specifically to Ambuja shares (sources conflated this with ACC's pledge release); the final status/amount of the CCI cartelization order; and an unconfirmed secondary-source claim of a long-term capacity target revision to 155 MTPA (only the 140 MTPA/FY28 target is independently corroborated). All of these should be checked on Screener or the company's latest filings before being stated as fact.
